design:
## Design tests

The refined visuals and the new placement rules were then read blind in six whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v019.md`), the four templates the v0.18 gate failed put in them: the reading walker in two busy tier-4 scenes with no wind, the stalking cat on a garden fence by a perched bird, the frying pan in a garden with no hose reel, and a runner in three. The reading walker read as reading and about to trip in both scenes, as reading "an open book" or "an open newspaper", with no reader saying papers in the wind; the cat on the fence as stalking, "about to pounce"; and the runner as running in all three, each time by the speed lines. The hose's jet and the sprinkler's arcs read as water, and the begging dog, the child pointing at the ball in the tree and the kick read as meant. No reader saw anyone against a lamp post, inside the swing frame or among the stall's legs.

Two remarks led to changes before the set was built: the runner's speed lines drawn over the pond (they now stay off the water), and the frying pan, read at first as "a grey can" before the reader added that its shape "looks more like a pan" (left as it is: on the bench both readers named a frying pan or a saucepan). A pram that seemed pulled rather than pushed is the pram pusher's pose, unchanged since v0.6.
intro: All four templates that failed the v0.18 gate pass the sixteenth screen: the reading walker read in full in all six of its pictures, three of them tier-4 ("she looks about to trip over it"), with no reader saying newspaper or papers in the wind; the runner read as running in all three, each time by its speed lines; the stalking cat on the fence and the frying pan away from the hose reel scored 0.944. No item in any of the 65 pictures was misread or missed outright: 750 of 760 scored items had full marks and ten had half points. The set scored 0.989 over all items (0.986 in v0.18), and its unintended oddities fell from 1.9 to 1.3 per picture. 60 of 64 templates pass the gate, as in v0.18: four others, each read in full in v0.18, fall short on a single half point in one picture: a bucket on a man's head at the back of a garden, read as "a tall blue hat"; a girl's drink on a bench, "something white ... as if drinking or eating"; a teenager's ice cream beside a boy who dropped his, "maybe to share it"; and a boy jumping just below a perched bird, read as reaching for it. `vision/flaws_v019.md` lists them with their fixes for v0.20.
screen: Across all 65 pictures only 10 of 760 scored items fell short of full marks (10 of 720 in v0.18), all by half a point, and none was misread (one in v0.18). In the set the six half points were in five pictures: in the tier-4 garden a boy jumping below a perched bird read as reaching for it, and the cat on the fence as "stalking the birds or just walking along" in the unsure section; in the tier-4 street whether the girl dropped her ice cream or the dog knocked it was left open; and in two park isomorphs a girl's drink was "something white", the boy beside the dropped ice cream was not said to have dropped it, and a teenager walking toward him with her cone was "maybe" going "to share it". Unintended oddities fell from 40 to 27 in the set and rose from 41 to 52 in the probes (44 probe pictures, 39 in v0.18). None of the v0.18 oddities came back as reported then: no one against a lamp post, inside the swing frame or among the stall's legs, no child beside the trunk under a ball in a tree, no kick read as a miss, no water read as a dotted line, no remark on the curly-haired boy's head. What the readers noticed instead: a watering can lying unused beside the frying pan (three probes) and water landing short of the flowers; the garden's wheelbarrow "very flat ... with no visible legs, looks tipped" (three probes); an empty swing blown through the frame's leg and other single overlaps; birds large next to people; wind that blows off a cap but leaves the trees and flowers still; and, again, goats out of place and a stall with nobody at it.
redrawn: The reading walker passes at 1.00 over six pictures and the runner at 1.00 over three. The stalking cat read in full on the grass and on the fence by its perched bird, "creeping along towards a blue bird", the unsure section adding "or just walking along" (a half point); the frying pan read as "a frying pan instead of a watering can" in two pictures and as "a grey round object held by a handle" in the third (a half point), and no reader said nozzle or wand. The child under a ball in a tree, the kick, the hose's jet and the sprinkler's soaked box all read with full marks; the begging dog, clear of the eater's legs, missed half a point only where its reader added "or barking".
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (54 in three, 5 in four, 1 in five, 3 in six, 1 in seven). Four fail, each on a single half point in one picture (the bucket hat on two), and all four read in full in v0.18: the bucket hat at the back of a garden probe, the drink on a bench in a park isomorph, the ice cream beside the dropped one in another, and the jump below a perched bird in the tier-4 garden. About five templates of the gate's movement between screens is reader variance (the v0.9 retest), but each of these has a cause in its picture that can be fixed. The v0.20 fixes: the bucket's handle and rim drawn, a coloured cup with a lid and straw, no ice-cream eater beside the dropped ice cream, and no bird above or beside a jumper's raised hands.
inspection: Inspecting the set added three more: no hand over the stall's crates of fruit (a runner's hand lay on the apples, as if snatching one); a runner and the runner's motion lines clear of the stall (drawn on its counter, the lines looked like marks on the wood); and the playground's seesaw never planned with its bench, right in front of which it stands (with the gap kept from thin parts nobody could sit there, and no busy playground with both could be placed).
